page: Microsoft Azure E16bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not contain graphics processing hardware, operating with zero GPUs.

A key structural attribute of the E16bs_v6 is its diskless configuration; the instance provides no integrated local ephemeral storage. System installations and data workloads rely entirely on external block storage, with native support for Azure Premium Storage tiers optimized for heavy remote I/O throughput. Network allocations for the instance do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring configured networking interfaces or virtual gateways for public routing.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance balances dedicated multi-core compute with an expanded memory footprint. While the absence of bundled local NVMe storage requires external disk provisioning, it prevents paying for unused local capacity in stateless or externally attached data topologies. The hardware configuration makes the E16bs_v6 suited for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
